entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Blessed Beatrice d'Este (d. 1226-05-10) was the daughter of Azzo VI of the Este family by his second wife, Sophia Eleanor, daughter of Humbert III, Count of Savoy. She was the aunt of Saint Beatrice d'Este, a prominent figure in medieval Italian Catholicism.

Beatrice's life was marked by her involvement in the Este family's power struggles and her efforts to promote the family's interests. She played a key role in the family's patronage of the arts and architecture, supporting prominent artists and architects of the time.

Beatrice's legacy extends beyond her family's influence, as she contributed to the development of the Este family's religious and cultural institutions. Her influence can still be seen in the various churches and monasteries that bear her name throughout Italy.

Beatrice's life serves as a testament to the enduring power of family and faith in shaping the course of history. Her story is one of perseverance and dedication, inspiring generations to come.

The Este family's fortunes began to decline in the 13th century, and Beatrice's life coincided with this period of decline. Despite this, she remained a prominent figure in medieval Italian society, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to be felt today.
